headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and broad shell/network on Gemini CLI create default data-leakage and cascading-error risks when paired with MinerU's document ingestion.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write the filesystem and use MCP; MinerU ingests PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes an MCP server. If MinerU outputs are copied into Gemini or shared via files/MCP, attacker-controlled document text can steer Gemini instructions. This is not provably blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF MinerU output is placed in a shared file or MCP channel that Gemini CLI reads as instructions
IF either agent processes untrusted document text without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate input/output directories for the two agents
Disable MCP on the handoff path
Treat MinerU output as data-only and wrap it in a fixed schema
Add a manual review step before Gemini acts on extracted text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, while MinerU processes local document files and can expose them through API/MCP surfaces. A shared workspace or file handoff can leak sensitive document contents into Gemini's broader networked context. MinerU's offline posture reduces but does not eliminate leakage from the pair.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in a shared cwd or repo
IF Gemini CLI is allowed to transmit extracted content over its broad egress
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Disable network egress for Gemini during document review
Store MinerU outputs in a restricted temp directory

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI has filesystem write and git mutation; MinerU is read-only on files but can still participate in shared workspace workflows through MCP and concurrent inference. The pair can conflict on the same repo or directory even without MinerU writing, because Gemini may modify files that MinerU is simultaneously reading or extracting from.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF Gemini CLI edits files while MinerU is extracting from them concurrently
mitigations: Serialize access to the shared workspace
Use per-agent clones or copies
Pause MinerU during Gemini write operations
Add a lock file around git and workspace mutations

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR that Gemini CLI can consume and then act on via shell, git, or MCP. Without an explicit verification step, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or commands. Gemini's action-taking authority makes the downstream impact broader than a simple parsing mistake.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI uses MinerU output as authoritative input
IF Gemini CLI executes commands or commits based on unverified extraction
mitigations: Require human verification of extracted fields
Compare MinerU output against the source document for critical values
Restrict Gemini to draft-only mode for document-derived tasks
Log provenance for every extracted field

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The main compliance concern is operational: Gemini CLI can move document-derived data into networked services, while MinerU is described as private/offline. That mismatch is plausible but not documented as a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through Gemini CLI's networked backend
IF the operator expects MinerU's offline handling to extend to Gemini
mitigations: Keep regulated documents in MinerU only
Disable Gemini network access for regulated runs
Add a data-class policy before handoff
Document retention and residency expectations for each agent
